title: DeepSeek Super-agent, explained with Napoleon's army (60 seconds)
description:
DeepSeek Super-agent explained in 60 seconds: one router agent takes your request and commands many AI worker agents, so you stop babysitting each coding agent yourself. Told with Napoleon's army.

Try it (open source, MIT, a research prototype and not an official DeepSeek product):
https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype
Ask your coding agent: "Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me."

Chapters
0:00 Napoleon's problem, and yours
0:17 Berthier, the chief of staff
0:27 How Super-agent works
0:47 The takeaway

The story: Napoleon led more than a hundred thousand soldiers and could not shout orders at each one. His fix was one man: Berthier, his chief of staff, who turned what Napoleon wanted into written orders for the corps. Super-agent works the same way: the router opens a ticket and hands it to a worker with its own session and its own folder. Many workers run at once, and the router speaks up only when you must decide or can use a result.

The takeaway: the limit isn't your agents. It's your attention.

Sources
Super-agent README and design docs: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype
"3 to 5 sessions" estimate by DeepSeek's team: https://letsdatascience.com/news/deepseek-proposes-experimental-super-agent-to-coordinate-mul-cc3cd380
Berthier, Napoleon's chief of staff: https://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/62795/Louis-Alexandre-Berthier-prince-de-Wagram
The Grande Armée in 1805: https://www.worldhistory.org/image/21911/la-grande-armee-napoleons-army-1804-1805/
The corps system: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grande_Arm%C3%A9e

"Take that hill." is an invented example order, not a quote.
Animation rendered from code. Voice by Kokoro, an open-source text-to-speech model.
